description: This case study is a nine-page FERC staff status report from December 2022 tracking the responses to the recommendations of the November 2021 FERC, NERC and Regional Entity joint staff report on the February 2021 cold weather outages in Texas and the South Central United States. Its bottom line slide states that ERCOT averaged 34,000 MW of generation outages for over two days and shed 23,418 MW of firm load, the largest in US history and the fourth cold-weather event in ten years that jeopardised bulk power system reliability. The document contains slides tracking key recommendations, with generator freeze protection standards filed on 28 October 2022, a winter readiness technical conference in April 2022 and a Texas Railroad Commission rule on gas facility preparedness plans adopted on 30 August 2022. Access: free PDF from the FERC website; no licence is stated. Coverage is the Texas and South Central event and its regulatory follow-up. Caveats: this is the status summary only; the 300-page staff report itself could not be opened from the cloud session, and progress reflects December 2022. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of coupled power and gas systems and policy follow-up, and it relates to the Texas 2021 blackout study and the 2011 Southwest cold event report catalogued here as case_study-texas-february-2021-winter-storm-blackout and case_study-ferc-nerc-southwest-cold-weather-event-february-2011-report.

name: The February 2021 Cold Weather Outages in Texas and the South Central United States: tracking of responses to recommendations (FERC, NERC and Regional Entity staff, December 2022)
outcomes: The bottom line slide states that ERCOT averaged 34,000 MW of generation outages for over two consecutive days, nearly half of its all-time winter peak load of 69,871 MW, and that the 23,418 MW firm load shed was the largest in US history; it was the fourth cold-weather event in ten years to jeopardise bulk power system reliability. Progress is tracked per recommendation: new generator freeze protection standards were filed with the Commission on 28 October 2022, a generator winter readiness technical conference was held on 27 and 28 April 2022, and the Texas Railroad Commission adopted a rule on gas facility cold weather preparedness plans on 30 August 2022.
